name: Gatineau Park
description: A massive forested park right on the city's edge, with lakes, the Eardley Escarpment cliffs, and dozens of trails for every fitness level.
why_visit_today: In fall this is one of the best spots for colorful foliage in the entire National Capital Region.
seasonal_notes: Open year-round; Champlain Lookout is especially popular in September-October
accessibility_notes: Main trails and Visitor Centre are wheelchair accessible, some trails are rocky and difficult

name: Luskville Falls
description: A steep but short trail alongside a small waterfall, leading to a panoramic view of the Ottawa Valley.
why_visit_today: A great option if you want a physical challenge rewarded with a view from the top in just a couple hours.
seasonal_notes: Best in spring (more water) and fall (foliage); can be slippery after rain
accessibility_notes: Steep rocky climb, not suitable for wheelchairs or limited mobility

name: Mer Bleue Bog Boardwalk
description: A unique ice-age bog with a wooden boardwalk trail crossing mossy hummocks, feeling like another planet.
why_visit_today: An easy flat walk for anyone who wants an unusual landscape without much physical effort.
seasonal_notes: Beautiful year-round, snowshoeing in winter
accessibility_notes: Boardwalk is flat and wheelchair-friendly for most of the route

name: Canadian Museum of History
description: One of Canada's largest museums, with exhibits on Indigenous history and colonization, plus a view of Parliament Hill across the river.
why_visit_today: A great option on a rainy or cold day, without giving up a view of the city.
seasonal_notes: Open year-round, hours may vary by season
accessibility_notes: Fully wheelchair accessible

name: National Gallery of Canada
description: The national art gallery, known for its striking glass architecture and the giant spider sculpture Maman at the entrance.
why_visit_today: A compact, inspiring trip in the heart of the city if you want culture without leaving town.
seasonal_notes: Open year-round
accessibility_notes: Fully wheelchair accessible

name: Wakefield Village
description: A small picturesque village with a covered bridge, local cafes and shops, along the Gatineau River.
why_visit_today: Perfect for an unhurried day of coffee, walking, and a Gatineau Park stop along the way.
seasonal_notes: Pleasant year-round, especially scenic in fall
accessibility_notes: Village center is largely walkable and flat

name: Vincent Massey Park
description: A calm park along the Rideau River with shaded picnic areas and easy trails.
why_visit_today: Good when you want relaxed time in nature without a long drive.
seasonal_notes: Best in spring, summer, and fall
accessibility_notes: Mostly flat, wheelchair accessible

name: Diefenbunker: Canada's Cold War Museum
description: An underground Cold War-era bunker turned museum — four floors below ground with original interiors.
why_visit_today: An unusual alternative to a regular museum, great for a rainy day and history buffs.
seasonal_notes: Open year-round, booking a tour in advance is recommended
accessibility_notes: Partially accessible, there's an elevator but not all areas are wheelchair-friendly

name: Parc Omega
description: A wildlife park where you can drive among free-roaming deer, bison, wolves, and bears.
why_visit_today: One of the few ways to see Canadian wildlife up close without heading far north.
what_to_bring: carrots (for feeding deer, sold on site)
seasonal_notes: Open year-round, animals are more active in the morning
accessibility_notes: Most of the route is driven by car, accessible for people with limited mobility

name: Major's Hill Park
description: A green hill in the heart of the city with one of the best views of Parliament Hill and the Rideau Canal.
why_visit_today: A quick way to catch a beautiful view and city atmosphere in about 20 minutes.
seasonal_notes: Good year-round, especially at sunset
accessibility_notes: Mostly flat lawn, wheelchair accessible

name: Rideau Canal Pathway
description: A historic UNESCO canal with pathways for walking and cycling in summer, and the world's largest skating rink in winter.
why_visit_today: A versatile option any time of year — from a summer bike ride to winter skating.
what_to_bring: bike or skates depending on season
seasonal_notes: The skating rink is usually open January through late February, weather dependent
accessibility_notes: Pathways are mostly flat and wheelchair accessible

name: Britannia Beach
description: An urban beach on the Ottawa River with sand, swimming areas, and grassy spots to relax.
why_visit_today: A simple summer option if you want water and sun without a long drive.
seasonal_notes: Swimming usually June through August, depending on water quality
accessibility_notes: Beach and surrounding area are accessible, but sand makes wheelchair movement difficult

name: Fitzroy Provincial Park
address: Dixon Point Rd, Fitzroy Harbour, ON K0A 1X0
description: A provincial park at the confluence of the Ottawa and Madawaska rivers, with trails, a beach, and camping areas.
why_visit_today: A good option for a calmer, less touristy nature day.
seasonal_notes: Open in warm season, usually May through October
accessibility_notes: Main areas accessible, some trails are uneven

name: Central Experimental Farm Arboretum
address: Prince of Wales Dr, Ottawa, ON K1A 0C6
description: A quiet arboretum with hundreds of tree and shrub species on the grounds of the Central Experimental Farm.
why_visit_today: A relaxed walk nearly downtown, great for resetting after a busy week.
seasonal_notes: Especially beautiful in spring (blossoms) and fall (foliage)
accessibility_notes: Flat paths, wheelchair accessible

name: Pink Lake Trail
address: Gatineau Park, near Old Chelsea, QC
description: A loop trail around a rare meromictic lake with an unusual green-turquoise water color.
why_visit_today: A short, moderate hike with a guaranteed beautiful water view.
seasonal_notes: Swimming is prohibited (fragile ecosystem), best in spring-fall
accessibility_notes: Trail has elevation changes, not wheelchair accessible

name: ByWard Market
address: 55 ByWard Market Square, Ottawa, ON K1N 9C3
description: A historic market with street vendors, local cafes, bakeries, and the famous BeaverTails pastries.
why_visit_today: A quick way to soak up city atmosphere and grab something local to eat.
seasonal_notes: Open year-round, more street vendors in summer
accessibility_notes: Generally wheelchair accessible, cobblestones can be uneven in places

name: Champlain Lookout
description: One of the region's best lookout points, with a view of the Ottawa Valley from the Eardley Escarpment.
why_visit_today: Views just steps from the parking lot — minimal effort, maximum payoff.
seasonal_notes: Peak popularity late September/early October for fall foliage
accessibility_notes: Lookout is wheelchair accessible right from the parking lot

name: Almonte
description: A cozy town with historic stone buildings, a small waterfall right in the town center, and local shops.
why_visit_today: A nice mix of architecture, water, and an unhurried day away from the city bustle.
seasonal_notes: Pleasant year-round
accessibility_notes: Town center is walkable and mostly flat

name: Canada Agriculture and Food Museum
address: 901 Prince of Wales Dr, Ottawa, ON K1A 0C7
description: A working farm-museum within city limits, where you can see cows, sheep, and horses and learn about Canadian agriculture.
why_visit_today: A great option for families with kids — a mix of animals and educational content.
seasonal_notes: Open year-round
accessibility_notes: Wheelchair accessible

name: Shirleys Bay
description: A little-known waterfront area on the Ottawa River, popular with birdwatchers and anyone looking for quiet.
why_visit_today: A genuine hidden gem without crowds — great for anyone tired of touristy trails.
seasonal_notes: Best birdwatching in spring and fall
accessibility_notes: Dirt trails, uneven, not wheelchair accessible

name: King Mountain Trail
address: King Mountain Trailhead, Gatineau Park, QC
description: One of Gatineau Park's most popular moderate loop hikes, ending at a lookout over the Ottawa Valley.
why_visit_today: A well-loved trail that balances a real workout with a rewarding payoff view.
seasonal_notes: Best spring through fall; can be muddy after rain
accessibility_notes: Moderate elevation gain, not wheelchair accessible

name: Wolf Trail (Sentier du Loup)
address: Gatineau Park, Old Chelsea sector, QC
description: A forested loop trail through mixed woods, one of the classic short-to-medium Gatineau Park hikes.
why_visit_today: A quieter alternative to the busier Gatineau Park trails, especially on weekends.
seasonal_notes: Beautiful in fall for foliage
accessibility_notes: Uneven forest trail, not wheelchair accessible

name: Hog's Back Falls
address: Hog's Back Rd, Ottawa, ON K1V
description: A small but powerful waterfall on the Rideau River, easily accessible right within the city.
why_visit_today: Real waterfall energy without leaving Ottawa — great for a quick nature fix.
seasonal_notes: Most dramatic during spring snowmelt
accessibility_notes: Paved paths near the falls, some viewpoints require stairs

name: Mackenzie King Estate Trails
description: Former estate of Canada's longest-serving Prime Minister, now a park with gardens, ornamental ruins, and easy walking trails.
why_visit_today: A gentle walk that mixes history and nature — good for a slower-paced day.
seasonal_notes: Tearoom typically open in summer months
accessibility_notes: Main paths are relatively flat and accessible

name: Carbide Willson Ruins
address: Gatineau Park, near Meech Lake, QC
description: Overgrown stone ruins of an old fertilizer plant beside a small waterfall, hidden inside Gatineau Park.
why_visit_today: One of the most photogenic hidden spots in the area — a mix of nature reclaiming history.
seasonal_notes: Best in spring/summer/fall, trail can be wet
accessibility_notes: Uneven trail with some rocky sections, not wheelchair accessible

name: Lac Philippe
description: One of Gatineau Park's larger lakes, with sandy beaches, canoe rentals, and surrounding hiking trails.
why_visit_today: A full-day nature escape combining swimming, paddling, and trails in one spot.
seasonal_notes: Best June through September
accessibility_notes: Beach areas partially accessible, trails are uneven

name: Andrew Haydon Park
description: A riverside park with sweeping lawns, a pond, and one of the best sunset views over the Ottawa River.
why_visit_today: A low-effort, high-reward spot for a relaxed evening walk and a great sunset.
seasonal_notes: Best spring through fall
accessibility_notes: Flat paved paths, wheelchair accessible

name: Merrickville
description: A well-preserved 19th-century town on the Rideau Canal, known as one of Canada's prettiest small towns.
why_visit_today: A longer drive that pays off with historic charm, boutiques, and canal-side walks.
seasonal_notes: Pleasant year-round, especially lively in summer
accessibility_notes: Town center is mostly flat and walkable

name: Dow's Lake
description: A small urban lake connected to the Rideau Canal, with pedal boat rentals and cafes right on the water.
why_visit_today: An easy, relaxed spot for coffee and a lakeside walk without leaving the city.
seasonal_notes: Pedal boats typically available May through September
accessibility_notes: Paved paths, wheelchair accessible

name: Mont Cascades area trails
description: Trails around a small mountain area near Cantley, with moderate hiking and a waterpark nearby in summer.
why_visit_today: Good combo destination if you want a hike with an option to cool off nearby afterward.
seasonal_notes: Best spring through fall
accessibility_notes: Moderate trail difficulty, not wheelchair accessible

name: Jack Pine Trail
description: An easy loop trail through forest and wetland in Ottawa's Greenbelt, popular with birdwatchers.
why_visit_today: A calm, easy hike that's still within city limits — perfect for a short escape.
seasonal_notes: Pleasant year-round, can be buggy in summer
accessibility_notes: Mostly flat gravel trail, largely accessible

name: Rockcliffe Lookout
description: A lookout over the Ottawa River and Gatineau Hills, tucked inside the leafy Rockcliffe Park neighborhood.
why_visit_today: A quiet, uncrowded view spot for a quick evening stop.
seasonal_notes: Pleasant year-round
accessibility_notes: Paved area near the lookout, wheelchair accessible
